title: Unemployment Benefit Claims — Valuing Holiday Pay Reported as Other Pay
content:
Where a claimant of Unemployment Benefit Claims certifies a week in which an employer paid holiday pay that the claimant cannot yet state in dollars, the holiday pay reported as other pay for that week is the regular hourly rate times the holiday hours times the holiday pay share, rounded to the cent.

## Elements of the valuation

| Element | Value |
|---|---|
| Source records | The certifications of the claimant's most recent earlier claim of the same program |
| History window | The last 3 calendar months, counted back from the handling date over certifications whose week ended within it |
| Regular hourly rate | The earlier claim's high-quarter wages divided by 520 quarter hours, rounded to the cent |
| Holiday hours | One working day of 8 hours |
| Holiday pay share | One |

The three elements are multiplied together, and the product is rounded to the cent.

## Worked example (hypothetical earlier claim)

The claimant's most recent earlier claim of the same program shows high-quarter wages of 9360.00.

- Regular hourly rate: 9360.00 divided by 520 is 18.00.
- Holiday pay: 18.00 times 8 hours times one is 144.00.

The holiday pay entered as other pay for the week is 144.00. For high-quarter wages of 8000.00 the rate is 15.38 (15.3846 rounded to the cent) and the holiday pay 123.04.
